predecessors.name: Kingdom of Lunda
predecessors.text: the Luapula valley east of the Lunda heartland

successors.name: British Africa
successors.text: 'The eastern shores became part of North-Eastern Rhodesia'

successors.name: Congo Free State
successors.text: 'the western shores went to the Compagnie du Katanga, the Congo Free State's agent'

capitals.name: Mwata Kazembe's capital (at Kanyembo in 1867-68; Mwansabombwe from the 1890s)

ledger.x: c. 1740: the Eastern Lunda kingdom of Kazembe is founded on the Luapula. 'Around 1740 the first Mwata, Ng'anga Bilonda' left Mwata Yamvo's kingdom 300 km west of the Luapula (list: '1740-5 I Ng'anga Bilonda').
1745-1760: Kanyembo Mpemba conquers the Shila in the Luapula valley.
1867: Msiri takes the west bank of the Luapula.
1894: the Luapula valley is divided between Britain and the Congo Free State.

wars.name: Msiri and Tippu Tip against Kazembe
wars.outcome: Msiri took the west bank of the Luapula by 1867 and, allied with Tippu Tip, 'attack[ed] and kill[ed] Mwata Kazembe in 1870'; Kazembe survived as a small state on the east side.

certainty.note: A tributary kingdom with no frontier given by the pages; the 1894 division of the valley (Britain and the Compagnie du Katanga) is the first agreed line but the page names no line.
